Name: Apache Tomcat RCE Vulnerability (Mar 2025) - Linux
description: Apache Tomcat is prone to a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability.
detection_method: Checks if a vulnerable version is present on the target host.
insight: The original implementation of partial PUT used a temporary le based on the user provided le name and path with the path separator replaced by '.'.
If all of the following are true, a malicious user is able to view security sensitive les and/or inject content into those les:
- writes enabled for the default servlet (disabled by default)
- support for partial PUT (enabled by default)
- a target URL for security sensitive uploads that is a sub-directory of a target URL for public uploads
- attacker knowledge of the names of security sensitive les being uploaded
- the security sensitive les also being uploaded via partial PUT

- writes enabled for the default servlet (disabled by default)
- support for partial PUT (enabled by default)
- application is using Tomcat's le based session persistence with the default storage location
- application includes a library that may be leveraged in a deserialization attack

Details: Apache Tomcat DoS Vulnerability (Feb 2023) - Linux OID:1.3.6.1.4.1.25623.1.0.104550 Version used: 2025-01-21T05:37:33Z
impact: Denial of service (application-level) via malicious upload or series of uploads due to unlimited number of request parts processed.
insight: Apache Tomcat uses a packaged renamed copy of Apache Commons FileUpload to provide the file upload functionality defined in the Jakarta Servlet specification.
Apache Tomcat was, therefore, also vulnerable to the Apache Commons FileUpload vulnerability CVE-2023-24998 as there was no limit to the number of request parts processed.
This resulted in the possibility of an attacker triggering a DoS with a malicious upload or series of uploads.

Name: Apache Tomcat Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (Dec 2019) - Linux
description: Apache Tomcat is prone to a privilege escalation vulnerability.
detection_method: Checks if a vulnerable version is present on the target host.
Details: Apache Tomcat Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (Dec 2019) - Linux OID:1.3.6.1.4.1.25623.1.0.143311 Version used: 2024-02-08T05:05:59Z
impact: A local attacker can manipulate the RMI registry to perform a man-in-the-middle attack to capture JMX credentials and then use them to gain complete control over the Tomcat instance.
solution: As a mitigation disable Tomcat's JmxRemoteLifecycleListener and use the built-in remote JMX facilities provided by the JVM.
insight: When Tomcat is configured with the JMX Remote Lifecycle Listener, a local attacker without access to the Tomcat process or configuration files is able to manipulate the RMI registry to perform a man-in-the-middle attack to capture user names and passwords used to access the JMX interface. The attacker can then use these credentials to access the JMX interface and gain complete control over the Tomcat instance.

detection_method: Sends an ICMP Timestamp (Type 13) request and checks if a Timestamp Reply (Type 14) is received.
Details: ICMP Timestamp Reply Information Disclosure OID:1.3.6.1.4.1.25623.1.0.103190
Version used: 2025-01-21T05:37:33Z
impact: This information could theoretically be used to exploit weak time-based random number generators in other services.
solution: Disable the support for ICMP timestamp on the remote host completely
Protect the remote host by a rewall, and block ICMP packets passing through the rewall in either direction (either completely or only for untrusted networks)
insight: The Timestamp Reply is an ICMP message which replies to a Timestamp message. It consists of the originating timestamp sent by the sender of the Timestamp as well as a receive timestamp and a transmit timestamp.
